projects.title: Unobravo Redesign
projects.description: A research-led redesign of Unobravo's website and app, the Italian online therapy platform, to make the service easier to understand and trust.
projects.introText: Unobravo connects people with therapists over video call. Its website tried to be a marketing page, a guide and an onboarding flow at once, and the app offered no explanation of the service at all. I redesigned both, from interviews to a tested Figma prototype.
projects.middleText: The research combined interviews across three age groups, a competitor study of Serenis, expert reviews and think-aloud testing. It surfaced nine usability issues: an overwhelming "how it works" page, calls to action that pushed people into the questionnaire before they understood the service, opaque therapist matching, scheduling that ignored stated preferences, a full test to repeat just to change therapist, no way to compare profiles, hidden pricing and privacy information, and an app whose navigation was buried in a sidebar.
projects.conclusionText: Over three iterations the design added a calmer home page, a real dashboard with the next appointment and pricing, three therapist proposals with a "why you match" explanation, filters to compare profiles, and a way to change therapist by only updating preferences. In the summative test of the final version, all four participants completed every task with no errors, and the average SUS score rose from 75 on the original product to 91.25.

aboutpara: I'm Alice, an anthropologist and digital humanities expert based in Amsterdam, blending critical research with creative technologies across cultural analysis, web development, and interactive design.

resume.description: I work at the intersection of culture, technology, and design, weaving together critical research and creative experimentation. With a background in cultural anthropology and a strong foundation in digital humanities, my projects range from interactive archives and feminist data visualizations to live-coded performances and augmented reality design. Whether I’m mapping digital territories, building ontologies of cognitive bias, or glitching visual narratives in real time, I’m driven by curiosity and a commitment to inclusive, ethical tech. I enjoy working across media and disciplines — from semantic web development to storytelling with code — always with a reflexive, research-oriented approach.
